label: check-goal.cjs --all returns exit 0 while printing findings: the corpus branch returns on report.errors only (check-goal.cjs:703) whereas the single-packet branch returns 1 for findings with no errors (check-goal.cjs:714). Reproduced on /tmp/goalcorpus: parent-budget_findings=2 and ALL_EXIT=0.

The same packet yields a parent-budget finding in corpus mode and a silent 5/5 PASS in single-packet mode: corpus reports 'configured durable-slice budget could not be resolved' (check-goal.cjs:351) while the packet path routes the same check through runOneCheck (check-goal.cjs:641) and reports findings=0. The only mode that can see the condition is the mode whose exit code cannot fail (f-iter005-001).

create.sh resolves its templates from the target repository rather than its own location: TEMPLATES_BASE defaults to $REPO_ROOT/.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates (create.sh:2253, repeated at :1477 and :1665), so running the shipped script against another checkout fails with 'Templates directory not found at /private/tmp/.../.skilled/...' exit 1, while its shared libraries are sourced location-relative. SPECKIT_TEMPLATES_BASE is the undocumented escape hatch; it appears in no help text.
verify: cd /tmp && mkdir -p probe0 && cd probe0 && git init -q && bash <repo>/.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh --short-name x --level 1 x; echo exit=$?

label: A fresh Level 1 and a fresh Level 2 packet from create.sh both PASS validate.sh --strict with 0 errors and 2 warnings, and one warning pair contradicts itself: CANONICAL_SAVE_PACKET_IDENTITY_NORMALIZED flags identity=scaffold/<name> versus identity=<name> while METADATA_DISK_PATH_CONSISTENCY passes with 'metadata paths carry the scaffold marker; the packet is not filed yet' on the same data, and MEASURED_BEHAVIOR warns that the block is empty although no level-1 or level-2 template scaffolds it. Answers the first half of Q7: no hand edits are needed to pass.

The /doctor:update router and the release engine publish different action sets: the router resolves check|align|apply|rollback|record-base|compat (update.md:38) while the engine USAGE is check|align|decide|apply|rollback|record-base|unlock (release-update.cjs:54). compat is a YAML-only workflow and decide/unlock are internal, so the operator-facing list is correct; the real gap is that the router flag matrix (update.md:39-44) is a hand-maintained second copy of FLAG_SETS (release-update.cjs:62) with no cross-check, and the contract test reads update.md only to confirm each action owns a workflow YAML (doctor-update-contract.test.cjs:49). A new engine flag ships undocumented and no test notices.

check --offline reports aggregate status 'unknown' while it already knows the checkout position: the run returned exit 0 with upstream.status=unknown ('offline mode'), checkout.position=ahead, aheadBy=1, dirty=true and 30-plus classified units, so an air-gapped or hook caller cannot distinguish 'ahead and dirty' from 'cannot tell'. A separate upstreamStatus field, or a fallback to the checkout position, would keep both answers.

Answer to the untested-step half of Q6: every engine subcommand is referenced by release-update.test.cjs (check, align, decide, apply, rollback, record-base, unlock) and compat has its own unit plus integration test, so no action is unreferenced; the step with no test is the router-to-engine parity seam that f-iter005-005 shows drifting. This is reference coverage only, not behavioural coverage.

direction: release-update enumerating .skilled/skills/.state as a release unit is a defect
reason: enumerateUnits excludes only .skilled/skills/.state/doctor-update and .skilled/release (release-update.cjs:23-24, :537-538) and the code comment states that other .state folders ship tracked READMEs and stay units; git ls-tree v4.0.2.0 confirms those READMEs are tracked, so skill:.state is intended behaviour, not a bug.

direction: compat missing from the engine USAGE line means /doctor:update compat is broken
reason: compat is a YAML-only workflow that calls upgrade-legacy.mjs directly and uses release-update.cjs only for check (doctor-update-compat-action.yaml:36-39); the engine never needs a compat subcommand, so the KEPT finding is the unguarded flag-matrix duplication, not a broken action.
